page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory, translating to 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server utilizes 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor is equipped with 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and 8-bit integer operations.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with Geekbench single-core scores and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression rates placing in the top tier. However, multi-core and memory-intensive benchmarks show clear limitations. The Passmark memory score falls into the poor category, and uncached large-block read memory bandwidth is weak at 38.47 GB/sec. Multi-threaded decompression and multi-core stress-ng performance are also weak, reflecting the physical core constraint of this 2-core, 4-thread configuration.

This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highcpu-4 offers a dense compute-to-RAM ratio suitable for workloads that benefit from high single-thread execution speeds and specialized instruction sets, such as text processing, basic cryptography, and lightweight web serving. It is less suited for memory-bound databases, software compilation, or large-scale multi-threaded processing due to its constrained memory bandwidth and low physical core count.
